title: applied-ml-experiment-scratchpad-2026-03-15-samira
content:
Daily scratchpad - applied ML experiments (short notes)
Date: 2026-03-15
Owner: Samira Khan
Context: trying to get stable eval runs for 7B/13B candidates with AWQ/GPTQ -> measure latency, mem, quality regressions vs fp16 baseline. Quick notes and TODOs.

Top goals for today:
- Finalize prompt set for summarization eval (200 cases, mix of long docs + email snippets)
- Run quantized 4-bit AWQ on redwood-compat-7b and compare ROUGE + avg token latency
- Investigate increased hallucination on Q&A prompt after int4 conversion
- Add continuous batching config for dedupe scenario and test end-to-end latency

Work log / commands run:
- 09:15: pulled latest serving-runtime branch (pr 782) -> includes kernel selection tweak (pad alignment fix)
- 09:30: convert model -> tools/gptq/convert_awq.sh redwood-compat-7b fp16 -> int4 --group-size 64 --act-order
- 10:05: start eval harness (eval/summarization/run_eval.py) with batch_size=1, stream=false, max_new_tokens=256
  - seed=42, temperature=0.0 (deterministic), metric=ROUGE-L, chrF
- 11:20: observed OOM on 2xA100-40GB node when using per-request KV cache warmup (scratch: reduce kv_cache_prealloc to 0.6)

Quick results (first pass) - keep as rough numbers:
- Baseline: redwood-compat-7b fp16
  - ROUGE-L (200 examples): 36.8
  - avg token latency (hot path, local cluster): 9.8 ms/token
  - peak mem (infer): 18.2 GB

- AWQ int4 (group-size=64, per-channel symmetric) on same machine:
  - ROUGE-L: 35.1 (-1.7)
  - avg token latency: 7.2 ms/token (25% faster)
  - peak mem: 8.9 GB (approx 2x reduction)
  - notes: small degradation on numeric fidelity; hallucination cases increased on Q&A prompts (see below)

- GPTQ int4 (gptq-default) quick run:
  - ROUGE-L: 35.6 (-1.2)
  - avg token latency: 7.5 ms/token
  - peak mem: 9.4 GB
  - notes: slightly better quality than AWQ on long-context summarization but slower kernel

Observations / hypotheses:
- AWQ gives best perf but larger drop on factuality -> maybe outlier noise from quantization of final output layers or softmax scale mismatch. Need to inspect per-layer quant stats and outlier activation histograms.
- Kernel selection: current runtime picks fused attention kernel for seq_len<=512; our summarization cases hit 1024 sometimes and fall back to slower path. Consider enabling multi-kernel fallback or pad-to-512 technique.
- Continuous batching is currently set to max_batch_wait_ms=8; could increase to 12-15 ms for throughput experiments (trade-off with latency SLO).

Prompt set notes (examples):
- Summarization (long_doc -> concise email):
  "Write a short, professional email summarizing the following conversation and action items:
   <DOCUMENT>"
- Q&A (facts):
  "Based on the passage below, answer the question using only the facts in the passage. If the answer is not present, say 'Insufficient information'. Passage: <DOC> Question: <Q>"
- Dedupe / reranking test:
  - prompt: "Given these candidate completions, return the top-1 non-repetitive answer and a confidence score (0-1)."

Failure cases / tickets to open:
- hallucination spike on Q&A after AWQ: collect 20 examples where baseline answer != AWQ answer; add to ticket. (JIRA-ML-1287)
- OOM on prealloc with large KV cache on 40GB nodes -> add a config guard in runtime to fallback to dynamic allocation when memory headroom < X

TODO (short):
- [ ] run per-layer quant stats for AWQ and save plots (activations + weight hist)
- [ ] rerun GPTQ with group-size=128 and compare
- [ ] add hashing-based dedupe cache for candidate reranking experiment
- [ ] add test harness for latency SLO simulation (p50/p95/p99)
- [ ] sync with Jordan on canary rollout config for dedicated cluster (meeting Thurs)

Notes to self (random):
- remember to push small patch to PR #782: fix pad-to-multiple-of-8 bug in matmul wrapper
- link to eval dashboard: https://internal.redwood/console/evals/summary?run=2026-03-15-7b-awq
- keep seed fixed across runs to avoid sampling differences when computing ROUGE differences

Quick micro-profiling (local):
- run: python -m torch_profiles.profile_token --model redwood-compat-7b-awq --seq 1024 --tokens 512
  - result (rough): avg forward time per token 6.9 ms; attention kernel 45% of time; lm_head 18%

Open questions / next experiments:
- Is hallucination correlated with specific tokens in input distribution? need token-level KL vs baseline on softmax logits.
- Try mixed-precision: AWQ weights + fp16 activations (partial quant) -> should reduce some degradation?

Small reminders:
- Prep slides for demo to product (Tue): show latency vs cost savings & 5 example failure modes
- Add a short note to confluence EVAL-342 about recommended default quant profile (AWQ group-size=64 was our current best trade-off)

End of scratchpad.
(Will iterate and convert to a proper PR/notes when stable)
